institutionName: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Norway's a beautiful  country. i wanted to be able to study on an academic level similar to, or above, what i had at home, while being able to spend my free time in nature

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: i came for good courses, mountains and norwegians, and i found good courses, mountains and norwegians

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I got information regarding intro-week and courses from emails and intro-events and meetings. I experienced some exchange students not getting all the necessary emails, so it's really important to talk to other exchange students about their plans and schedules, so you don't miss out on any good events or meetings :)

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: ESN had many introduction events, and i joined the study association from my faculty. This was a great help in finding people who knew about the city, events and courses

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: not everyone got the necessary information

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: make sure you have good public transportation to and from your place. I lived in upper-Risvollan and paid 4500 NOK p. month.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: signing up for the courses was easy, but getting permission to take the courses and getting them pre-approved at the host university was really an issue

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You didn't have to finalize registration of courses till september, so you could use august to try different courses before you decide (you still have to get every course pre-approved

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: emails and guides on the NTNU website

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes i wanted, even though i had to send several emails to the staff at the receiving university

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
If you get rejected from a course you should be able to take. remember to inquire as to why you've been rejected and if there are ways of getting onto the course.
You don't have to finalize registration for courses until 1st of september so you can try to attend more courses i august before you finally decide on courses to continue with.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
KLH3101 Obesity, got turned into a self study course due to low attendance (only 3 people were taking the course) which i haven't tried before at UCPH and NEVR2030 Neuroscience was entirely through zoom.

otherwise my courses followed similar structure as UCPH

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
MOL3023 Molecular Medical Bacteriology (MA)
MOL3005 Immunology (MA)
KLH3101 Obesity: Epidemiology, Pathophysiology and Consequenses (BA)
NEVR2030 Condensed Introduction to Neuroscience (BA)

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
MOL3023 Molecular Medical Bacteriology (MA)
- Interesting course going through most common bacterial infections and bioinformatic methods of detection and sequencing. i chose this course for the bioinformatics
MOL3005 Immunology (MA)
- I really recommend this course. well structured and interresting
KLH3101 Obesity: Epidemiology, Pathophysiology and Consequenses (BA)
- A broad understanding of obesity and a visit to an obesity clinic where we got to scan our own bodies. sadly the course become self-study
NEVR2030 Condensed Introduction to Neuroscience (BA)
- when it says introduction, it really is introduction. all lectures through zoom were recorded which gave a great amount of freedom for planning trips

questions.answer: food and alchohol is expensive. There are also a lot of payments at the start of the semester for ESN and student organisations like NTNUI and SIT

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and alchohol was more expensive than i had expected. sports and outdoor equipment was really cheap at the store called Sports Outlet

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Join NTNUI and SIT for sports and fitness clubs, join your student organisation or Samfundet for social stuff and parties :)

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: NTNUI is the sports organisation for NTNU and they have alot of different groups and sports that you can join. Samfundet is the social hub of NTNU and student life in Trondheim, be sure to check them both out.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Samfundet has a lot of great events through out the semester, be sure to keep track of their calendar and attend the events :)
NTNUI is really popular and a really good way of meeting new people in the city through sports. there are teams for both beginners and intermideates, so you can easily find a team for something you've never tried before or something you already are good at. remember to pay attention to the deadline for joining the NTNUI teams because the free spots are really sought after and can be gone in seconds after admission starts.
I would recomend spending a lot of time the first month attending different NTNUI events, so that you are ready for when the different clubs and teams have admission. remember to attend the different BBQs that NTNUI has and the "Aktiv Uke".

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Bymarka is a great place for easy afternoon hikes or longer weekend trips. it's easy to get there with bus and tram, and cheap since you don't have to rent a car. Remember to het out while the sun is still there.
go visit some of the larger nature parks like Trollheimen or jotunheimen, amazing areas if you want propper mountains to climb.
I saw the most beautiful northern lights in the polar circle in Lofoten, and i would really recommend going there if you have the time.
Røros also has a very lovely christmas market you can visit in the start of december.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
quite easy as a dane. it's a bit of a 50/50 if the norwegians can understand your danish, so i tried to learn Norwegian, which worked out pretty well. 
Norwegians students drink a lot. Even though it's really expensive, it's a good way of getting close to them, since they can be a little reclusive.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
1. Volunteer at the student organisations and go to their parties
2. Get them drunk

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I ended up not getting a bike while i was in Trondheim as the city didn't really accomodate for it. This made it quite dificult to get home at night since the busses didn't go after 00:30 on week days

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Norwegians are very sweet people and they have the most beautiful landscape

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be as active as possible during the start of the semester. that's where you have the chance to sign up for all the student organisations.

Taking 4 different courses is a lot of work during exam time and during the semester. Might be a good idea to take 2 or 3 courses.

The student life is amazing but remember to get out into the nature parks around the city and in the rest of the country.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember remember remember to talk to other exchange students about exchange, so you are sure there is nothing important that you miss out on.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Northern lights in Lofoten and making friends with norwegians and other exchange students.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding the time for all the things i wanted to do. Especially balancing Studying and all the other things i wanted to do.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
